items.front: Science vs Technology vs Innovation?
items.back: Science = knowledge of nature; Technology = applying it; Innovation = successful use/market adoption. Invention ≠ innovation.
items.examPoint: Science vs technology vs innovation — distinction and relevance to daily life
items.source: DST STI framework

items.front: Which article makes 'scientific temper' a Fundamental Duty?
items.back: Article 51A(h) — develop scientific temper, humanism & spirit of inquiry; added by 42nd Amendment, 1976.
items.examPoint: Scientific temper — Article 51A(h) fundamental duty (42nd Amendment, 1976)
items.source: Constitution of India

items.front: India's four S&T policies + years (in order)?
items.back: SPR 1958 (Nehru), TPS 1983 (self-reliance), STP 2003, STIP 2013 (2% GERD, top-5). Draft STIP 2020 = 5th, not notified.
items.examPoint: Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2013 (STIP) — 2% GERD goal, top-5 aspiration
items.source: DST

items.front: ANRF (2023) — what did it replace and who chairs it?
items.back: Replaced SERB; apex research funder; ~₹50,000 cr (2023-28, ~₹36k cr private); PM is ex-officio President of Governing Board.
items.examPoint: ANRF Act 2023 — replaced SERB, Rs 50,000 crore, private funding, PM-chaired board
items.source: ANRF Act 2023

items.front: Three departments of the Ministry of Science & Technology?
items.back: DST (1971), DBT (1986), DSIR (parent of CSIR). DAE is separate — directly under the PM.
items.examPoint: Ministry of Science & Technology — three departments (DST, DBT, DSIR)
items.source: dst.gov.in

items.front: CSIR — founding year, parent, size?
items.back: Founded 1942; under DSIR; network of ~37 labs (NPL, NCL, CCMB, IICT). One of world's largest public R&D bodies.
items.examPoint: CSIR — founded 1942, about 37 laboratories, under DSIR
items.source: csir.res.in

items.front: DAE — year, reports to whom, founder?
items.back: 1954; works directly under the Prime Minister; shaped by Homi J. Bhabha. Units: BARC, IGCAR, NPCIL.
items.examPoint: Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) — 1954, under the Prime Minister, Homi Bhabha
items.source: dae.gov.in

items.front: National Quantum Mission — year and outlay?
items.back: Approved 2023; ₹6003.65 crore (2023-24 to 2030-31); four hubs: computing, communication, sensing, materials.
items.examPoint: National Quantum Mission 2023 — Rs 6003.65 crore (2023-24 to 2030-31)
items.source: PIB

items.front: RDI Scheme (2025) — corpus and purpose?
items.back: ~₹1 lakh crore corpus; low-cost finance for private-sector R&D in sunrise/strategic sectors. Complements (not replaces) ANRF.
items.examPoint: RDI Scheme 2025 — Rs 1 lakh crore corpus for private-sector R&D
items.source: PIB 2025

items.front: India's GERD; who publishes GII and India's rank?
items.back: GERD ~0.64% of GDP (target was 2%). GII published by WIPO; India 39th (2024), 38th (2025); tops lower-middle-income group.
items.examPoint: India's R&D spend (GERD) about 0.64% of GDP and Global Innovation Index rank
items.source: DST; WIPO GII

items.front: ONOS — when operational and via which agency?
items.back: One Nation One Subscription operational 1 Jan 2025; central e-journal access via INFLIBNET (UGC); ~₹6,000 cr for 2025-27.
items.examPoint: One Nation One Subscription — operational Jan 2025, Rs 6,000 crore, INFLIBNET
items.source: PIB

items.front: AP trap: which Hyderabad labs are NOT in Andhra Pradesh?
items.back: CCMB, IICT, NGRI stayed in Telangana (Hyderabad) after 2014. AP has SDSC-SHAR, NARL Gadanki, IIT/IISER Tirupati, IIPE Vizag, AIIMS Mangalagiri.
items.examPoint: CCMB is in Hyderabad (Telangana), not AP — common trap
items.source: CSIR; ISRO; AP institutions

items.front: When did the ANRF Governing Board hold its first meeting, and who chaired it?
items.back: September 2024, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
